card.situation: VA Technology Acquisition Center is seeking sources for Cybersecurity Architecture and Engineering Services (COSE) — a 54-month enterprise engagement covering Zero Trust design, security engineering, DLP, AI governance, and supply chain risk management for VA information systems.\nThis Sources Sought reached the owner because Sooner Systems is SDVOSB-eligible and holds NAICS 541512, matching the solicitation's set-aside and NAICS code.
reasons_for: Sooner Systems is SDVOSB-eligible under FAR 19.14, directly matching the solicitation's set-aside, so the firm clears the status gate [profile: set-asides SDVOSBC, SBA].

The firm's 22 cleared staff, 24x7 NOC, and vulnerability management capability (ACAS/Nessus) partially satisfy operational security and staffing requirements [07b8aa34-8fe148c3-p1-943fb8a7, 07b8aa34-8fe148c3-p1-2d4c22d7, 07b8aa34-8fe148c3-p1-87a028f6].

Responding to this RFI costs only a capability statement and could establish a relationship with VA TAC for a future full solicitation, with no proposal or price at risk [notice type: Sources Sought].
reasons_against: The firm holds no GSA MAS contract with SIN 54151HACS, which the notice explicitly states is required for award eligibility — a hard disqualifier that a capability statement cannot cure [07b8aa34-descript-p0-b83409aa, 07b8aa34-5453b3d0-p1-21f4608f].

Nineteen of 37 requirements are gaps, including enterprise security architecture, Zero Trust design, threat modeling, DLP, AI/LLM governance, and supply chain risk management — the core technical scope of the contract [07b8aa34-8fe148c3-p1-8fe148c3, 07b8aa34-8fe148c3-p1-4d4c11d9, 07b8aa34-8fe148c3-p1-924d1598].

The firm has only one credible past-performance match (FAA, $1.65M), failing the internal two-match bid gate, and the contract's 54-month enterprise VA scope far exceeds the firm's largest known contract at $2.1M [profile: past performance, FAA Mike Monroney Aeronautical Center; owner rule ss-pp].

drafts.capability_statement:
Sooner Systems LLC — Capability Statement
VA-26-00064748 | DJ01 Cybersecurity Architecture and Engineering Services

Sooner Systems LLC is a Service-Disabled Veteran-Owned Small Business (SDVOSB) headquartered in Norman, Oklahoma, operating under NAICS 541512. We are verified under SBA VETCert and are fully eligible to compete under the SDVOSB set-aside for this requirement.

Core Cybersecurity Capabilities:
• Risk Management Framework (RMF) and Authority to Operate (ATO) documentation support
• Vulnerability management using ACAS/Nessus; STIG compliance assessment and remediation
• Security Operations Center (SOC) services: SIEM, SOAR, incident response, and 24x7 NOC operations from our Norman, OK facility
• Network administration and cybersecurity support across federal environments
• Firewall management, ISSO support, and network security monitoring
• Microsoft 365 and Azure administration, including encrypted communications compliant with FIPS 140-2 successor standards

Workforce:
Sooner Systems maintains a bench of 22 personnel holding active Secret clearances, with Security+ and ITIL 4 certifications across the team. We can deliver a staffing plan and employee roster within three business days of award.

Relevant Past Performance:
• FAA Mike Monroney Aeronautical Center (2021–2024, $1.65M): network administration and cybersecurity support including RMF, ATO, vulnerability management, ACAS, STIG, SOC, SIEM, SOAR, incident response, and firewall operations.

Sooner Systems welcomes the opportunity to discuss how our operational cybersecurity capabilities and cleared workforce can support VA's enterprise security mission.

Contact: [Owner name, title, phone, email]
questions_for_co: GSA MAS SIN 54151HACS eligibility — The notice states that either the Prime Offeror or the JV entity itself must hold an active GSA Multiple Award Schedule contract with SIN 54151HACS to be eligible for award. Will VA consider responses from firms that do not currently hold SIN 54151HACS but are actively pursuing it, or is an active SIN a firm prerequisite at the time of RFI response and any subsequent solicitation? [07b8aa34-descript-p0-b83409aa]

Teaming and subcontracting for architecture roles — The PWS requires an Enterprise Security Architect Lead and Cybersecurity Engineer III. May a prime SDVOSB satisfy these labor category requirements through a subcontractor or teaming partner, and if so, what percentage of work must the SDVOSB prime self-perform to remain compliant with the set-aside limitations on subcontracting? [07b8aa34-8fe148c3-p1-5309a60d]

BETSIE program scope and documentation — The PWS references BETSIE program performance reporting against 97% asset coverage and data accuracy thresholds on a 30-day rolling average. Could the CO provide additional context on what the BETSIE program entails, what data sources feed it, and whether incumbent or transition documentation will be available to an incoming contractor? [07b8aa34-8fe148c3-p1-e0b6053d]

AI and LLM governance requirements — The PWS requires evaluation of AI tool outputs for Trustworthy AI and Unbiased AI compliance, as well as LLM benchmark scoring and training process documentation. Does VA anticipate providing a government-furnished AI governance framework or policy baseline, or is the contractor expected to develop these standards from scratch? [07b8aa34-8fe148c3-p1-50f9b87e, 07b8aa34-8fe148c3-p1-924d1598]

Contract vehicle requirement at solicitation stage — The notice references existing contractual vehicles (GWAC, FSS) as an evaluation or eligibility factor. Will the forthcoming solicitation require an active contract vehicle at time of proposal submission, or will VA accept responses from firms without a current GWAC or FSS schedule? [07b8aa34-66ee78f4-p1-db99d3b8]

DLP optional task sequencing — The PWS states that DLP Enterprise Functional Requirements and Use Cases are due 60 calendar days after the initial 6-month Optional Task award. Is the DLP optional task expected to be exercised at the start of the base period, or is it truly optional and exercised at VA's discretion? Understanding the likelihood and timing of this task would help small businesses assess staffing and teaming needs. [07b8aa34-8fe148c3-p1-22f647d0]

reader.scope_summary: The VA is acquiring Cybersecurity Architecture and Engineering Services (COSE) to ensure VA information systems, technologies, and enterprise platforms are designed and implemented in accordance with cybersecurity best practices, federal security frameworks, Zero Trust principles, and VA enterprise security policies. The Contractor shall provide Enterprise Security Architecture and Design, Security Standards and Requirements Development, Enterprise Security Engineering, Secure Enterprise Baseline Configuration Management, and related subject matter expertise. The Period of Performance shall consist of a 6-month base period, four 12-month option periods and four optional tasks for a total of 54 months.
quotes: For clarification: either the Prime Offeror or the JV entity itself must hold an active General Services Administration Multiple Award Schedule contract with Special Item Number 54151HACS to be eligible for award.

The Contractor shall provide Enterprise Security Architecture and Design services to ensure VA information systems, technologies, and enterprise platforms are designed and implemented in accordance with cybersecurity best practices, federal security frameworks, Zero Trust principles, and VA enterprise security policies.
PERFORMANCE PERIOD The Period of Performance (PoP) shall consist of a 6-month base period, four 12-month option periods and four optional tasks for a total of 54 months.

Table 5.5 -1 Modular Delivery Optional Task Structure Modular Task | Size | Section | Team Structure | PoP | Exercise Frequency Cybersecurity Architecture and Engineering | Small | 5.2 | Enterprise Security Architect, Lead (1), Cybersecurity Engineer III (1), Security Specialist I (1) | 90 days | Up to 4 times per period Cybersecurity Architecture and Engineering | Medium | 5.2 | Enterprise Security Architect, Lead (1), Cybersecurity Engineer III (3), Cybersecurity Analyst Expert (1) | 90 days | Up to 4 times per period Cybersecurity Architecture
The Contractor shall perform risk analyses and architecture gap analyses to evaluate compliance with VA and federal security policies, standards, and frameworks.

The Contractor shall continuously evaluate emerging cybersecurity technologies, methodologies, automation capabilities, and artificial intelligence (AI)-enabled solutions applicable to the performance of this contract.
The Contractor shall provide a Staffing Plan due three business days after contract award.
The Staffing Plan and Contractor Staff Roster shall be in Microsoft Excel format and submitted via encrypted email or another FIPS 140-2 (or successor) compliant method.

Within 3 business days after award, the Contractor shall provide a roster of Contractor and Subcontractor employees to the COR to begin their background investigations in accordance with the PAL template artifact.
Tasks under this Task Order (TO) shall be performed at Contractor facilities, as well as the VA Central Office (VACO) Government facility for meetings and coordination as needed.
The Contractor staff shall be available to coordinate with VA-COSE staff on normal Federal Government workdays and shall be responsive between the core hours of 8:00am and 5:00pm EST.
